absent: Head of CPU-form table before cgroup hooks including selection, queueing, dispatch, tick and task lifecycle signatures and guarantees
Value definitions for SCX_OPS flags, SCX_ENQ variants, SCX_SLICE_DFL, SCX_REENQ_MAX_REPEAT, SCX_CID_SHARD_MAX_CPUS, SCX_RESCUE_DISABLE and SCX_OPS_NAME_LEN
Layouts of runqueue extension, dispatch queue, cmask, exit info, attach and detach argument blocks, acquire and release argument blocks, dump context and scheduler object
Semantics of helpers scx_bpf_sub_caps, grant, revoke, cid_override, cidperf_set, events, queue_sync_ecaps, scx_process_sync_ecaps and rescue decay
Algorithms for slice refill and clamping, DSQ insertion and bouncing, kick and preempt delivery, bypass activation, rescue admission and overload ejection
Behavior when group scheduling or sub-scheduling options are disabled and sysfs exposure beyond the root operations file

findings.text: Tail of the CPU-form scheduler operations publishes three cgroup controls named cgroup_set_weight, cgroup_set_bandwidth and cgroup_set_idle. Each receives the affected cgroup and new configuration, namely a bounded weight, bandwidth period quota and burst, or an idle flag. Bandwidth handling originates from the cpu maximum interface and may sleep, with entitlement derived from quota over period and burst describing temporary excess, while concrete shaping stays scheduler defined.

The same operations table publishes sub-scheduler management named sub_attach, sub_detach, sub_caps_updated and sub_ecaps_updated. Attachment reports acceptance with zero and refusal with a negative error number. Shard notices carry a changed mask plus changed capability bits, while effective notices carry an identifier plus previous and current effective bits. The shard notice may grant or revoke on children, and the effective notice may insert or move tasks.

A CID-form operations table named sched_ext_ops_cid offers parallel coverage for identifier based scheduling. It provides hooks such as select_cid, enqueue, dequeue, dispatch, tick, runnable, running, stopping, quiescent, yield, core_sched_before, set_weight, set_cmask, update_idle, init_task, exit_task, enable, disable, dump, dump_cid and dump_task, optional group controls prefixed cpuctl, sub-scheduler hooks, cid_online and cid_offline, plus init_cids, init and exit.

Hotplug and bring-up entries comprise cpu_online, cpu_offline, cid_online, cid_offline, init_cids, init and exit. Online and offline report a single processor or identifier changing state. Layout finalization runs after the default identifier arrangement and before capability and shard commitment, allowing custom arrangement only for CID-form schedulers. Initialization signals success with zero, while teardown always runs including after failed initialization to convey diagnostic detail.

Weight, bandwidth and idle entries execute against the parent scheduler of the target cgroup rather than the scheduler directly attached to it. Attachment entries decide admission of a child scheduler, detachment releases it, shard capability entries observe merged changes without direction, and effective capability entries observe per-processor committed changes while dispatch activity is possible.

Configuration state closing both operations tables holds fields named dispatch_max_batch, flags, timeout_ms, exit_dump_len, hotplug_seq, cid_shard_size, rescue_bandwidth_ppt, rescue_quantum_us, sub_cgroup_id, name and priv. The CPU form appends retired hooks cpu_acquire and cpu_release after the private pointer, while the CID form appends an empty trailing marker named __end instead. Name is a fixed length array and the private pointer is reserved.

Event accounting named scx_event_stats contains only signed sixty four bit integers, one per condition. Covered conditions include fallback processor choice, offline local queue bounce, retained execution, skipped exiting and migration-disabled queueing, immediate requeue, repeated requeue without intervening run, default slice refill, slice clamping and denial, bypass duration dispatch and activation, foreign insertion, descendant bypass dispatch, forced admission, preempt kick requeue and performance denials, and rescue entry.

Dispatch staging uses scx_dsp_buf_ent to associate a task pointer with queue sequence, destination queue identifier, slice length, virtual time and enqueue flags. Container scx_dsp_ctx pairs a runqueue pointer with cursor and task count plus a variable length array of entries. Helper scx_deferred_reenq_local pairs a list linkage with flag bits for postponed local requeue work.

Per-processor scheduler state scx_sched_pcpu starts with a scheduler backpointer and flag word, followed by four processor masks for kick, idle-conditional kick, preempt and wait plus a linkage for pending kick processing. Under sub-scheduling it adds effective capability bits, a lock-free sync linkage, an idle renotify marker, last reported effective bits, and decaying rescue consumption with timestamp. It then carries event statistics, deferred requeue state and a bypass queue with host sequence, ending with an embedded dispatch context that must remain final. Node state scx_sched_pnode holds only a global queue.

Shard capability state uses scx_caps_updated to combine a spin lock, accumulated capability bits, an arena output mask pointer, an in-flight list linkage and inline mask storage accessed as a mask object. Container scx_pshard combines its own spin lock, a scheduler backpointer, an embedded pending update object, one inline mask per capability, and trusted base index plus identifier count used to reinitialize writables whose live range may shift before deferred release.

Ordering constraints require every normal operation to precede the processor online hook, every hotplug operation to precede layout finalization, and every operation hook to precede configuration fields. Retired acquire and release hooks reside beyond the operation index end and must be tested directly rather than through generic presence helpers. CID and CPU tables keep identical configuration layout, the dispatch context stays last in per-processor state due to its flexible tail, and the empty marker stays last in the CID table for compile-time verification.

Cgroup attribute ownership stays with the parent scheduler, so weight, bandwidth and idle changes for a child are presented to the parent. That parent may have no prior initialization record for the child when the child sits at a sub-scheduler boundary, in which case knowledge of the child arrives through attachment rather than through initialization.

Four capabilities occupy successive bit positions starting at zero for immediate insertion, normal insertion, preemption and performance control. Derived combinations denote the full set, the minimal usable subset aliased to immediate insertion, and the subset whose withdrawal orphans queued work. A helper named scx_for_each_cap_bit iterates over set bits by repeatedly extracting the lowest set position and clearing it.

The flag word and effective capability copy are owned by the local processor and mutated only while holding its runqueue lock during queued synchronization, though the effective copy may be sampled without the lock through a single atomic read. Target per-capability masks are serialized by the shard lock, while the coalescing accumulator has its own lock. Decaying rescue consumption and its timestamp are touched only under the local runqueue lock.

Kick targeting state is owned per scheduler per processor. Recording a kick stores destination sets in that scheduler slot and links the slot onto the processor runqueue pending list, which a single deferred work item per processor later walks to perform attributed wakeups for each scheduler.

A processor reporting online has not yet performed queueing or dispatch nor executed work affiliated with other processors, and a processor reporting offline will perform no such activity afterwards. Layout finalization occupies a distinct phase between default arrangement construction and capability and shard commitment, with custom arrangements honored solely for identifier-form schedulers and disregarded otherwise.

Shard capability notification allows at most one outstanding delivery per shard, merging all changes since the prior delivery into one mask and bit set without indicating set versus clear, requiring an explicit query for current state. It is emitted asynchronously after recording and may precede hardware effect, serving bookkeeping and propagation to children. Effective notification fires per identifier once committed on that processor, in dispatch context under the runqueue lock, updating the last-reported snapshot and permitting queue manipulation.

Rescue execution proceeds serially per processor with admissions throttled to respect a bandwidth fraction and a per-rescue time quantum. Default pacing yields one short rescue at a much longer interval, crowded waiters divide the quantum with a lower bound, and an unresponsive rescue escalates toward forced execution. Sustained overload selects the child with the greatest decaying consumption for ejection.

Load-time and run-time hazards include rejection when a nonzero hotplug sequence mismatches the enable-time sequence, mandatory teardown after failed bring-up for diagnostics, rejection of empty or malformed scheduler names, clipping or rejection of oversized shard, bandwidth and quantum settings with silent elevation of unmeterably short quanta, ejection after unbounded requeue repetition without progress, silent dropping of foreign queue insertions, forced yet counted admission of pinned tasks lacking rights, and degraded or dropped kicks, preemptions, requeues and performance settings when rights are missing.

Numeric contracts fix weight between one and ten thousand, runnable wait default and ceiling at thirty seconds, zero dump length selecting thirty-two thousand seven hundred sixty-eight bytes, zero shard size selecting twenty-four identifiers with larger requests clipped to an architecture ceiling, zero rescue share selecting twenty parts per thousand with ceiling two hundred fifty and a distinct disable value, zero rescue quantum selecting five thousand microseconds with nonzero values limited to one thousand through one hundred thousand, and attachment identifiers above one requesting sub-scheduler mode.

Positional contracts place the bypassing marker at bit zero of per-processor flags, immediate, normal, preempt and performance rights at bit indexes zero through three, the operation range beginning at zero, the normal phase ending at the online hook index, the hotplug phase spanning online through layout finalization, and the overall table end coinciding with layout finalization.
